title: Bad-seed count for a nonzero input
statement: Fix a prime $p$ and let $v : \mathrm{Fin}\,\mathrm{width} \to \bbz/p$ be a nonzero vector. Consider families $S = (S_1,\dots,S_\ell)$ of subsets $S_k \subseteq \mathrm{Fin}\,\mathrm{width}$, indexed by $\mathrm{Fin}\,\ell$, and call such a family *bad* for $v$ if the value-level OR approximator $1 - \prod_k\bigl(1 - (\sum_{i \in S_k} v_i)^{p-1}\bigr)$ disagrees with the value-level OR detector $1 - \prod_k\bigl(1 - v_k^{\,p-1}\bigr)$. Then the number of bad families, multiplied by $2^\ell$, is at most the total number of families $S : \mathrm{Fin}\,\ell \to \mathrm{Finset}(\mathrm{Fin}\,\mathrm{width})$.
hypotheses_covered: S ranges over families (Fin ℓ → Finset (Fin width))
conclusion: (bad count) · 2^ℓ ≤ total number of families
